title: The Way Home
content:
Heading home. A whole year drifting abroad, yet it feels like a mere blink of an eye. Still, it is just me—shouldering my pack, setting off on the journey back.

The moment the final exam ended, the cacophony ceased. That instant of silence caught me off guard. Headphones on, an Americano in hand, a cigarette lit. I can’t tell if it’s the nicotine or the caffeine at work, but the world has never looked so bright. The Ferry (渡口) plays in my ears, and for a moment, I can’t distinguish joy from sorrow. Years ago, on another afternoon, I once danced to this very song.

Moments of tranquility are so precious, yet they are like a leaky wooden boat—eventually, they will be filled by new noise and sink. I keep clicking "Next," hoping the music will rescue me from this lonely vessel. Then, I stop. It’s "Black Butterfly." I don't understand why the melody is so tender, but that tenderness leaves me defenseless. I’ve never dared to face such gentleness before. Yes, I’m going home. Going home alone.

But this time is different. I embrace that tenderness without hesitation. A wave of heat brushes against my cheeks, coaxing a smile. Perhaps I’ve forgiven the world, or the world has forgiven me. I stop walking; behind me lies the fading glow of the sunset.

It’s getting late. I think it’s time to head back. I take off my headphones and dial her number.

In this Allegheny blue hour, it is no longer just me, shouldering my pack, heading home.
